question: If an agency is using an approved retroreflectivity-management method but a few individual signs temporarily fall below Table 2A-5, is the agency automatically out of compliance? Include the white-on-red thresholds relevant to STOP-type signs.
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. The mandatory requirement is to use an assessment or management method designed to maintain retroreflectivity at or above Table 2A-5 minimums; the MUTCD's Support text explicitly states that an agency using such a method remains in compliance even if some individual signs are temporarily below the minimums, though signs identified by the method as deficient should be replaced. For white-on-red signs such as STOP signs, Table 2A-5 requires minimum maintained levels of White ≥ 35 and Red ≥ 7 cd/lx/m², with a minimum sign contrast ratio of at least 3:1 (white retroreflectivity ÷ red retroreflectivity). Standards (mandatory): - "Public agencies or officials having jurisdiction shall use an assessment or management method that is designed to maintain sign retroreflectivity at or above the minimum levels in Table 2A-5." Guidance (recommended): - Except for signs identified in Paragraph 5, one or more of the methods described in "Maintaining Traffic Sign Retroreflectivity" (FHWA-SA-07-020, Revised 2013), or a method developed based on an engineering study, should be used to maintain sign retroreflectivity at or above the Table 2A-5 minimums; "Signs that are identified through the agency's method as being below the minimum levels should be replaced." Options (permitted): - Highway agencies may exclude the following from the retroreflectivity maintenance guidelines: (A) Parking, Standing, and Stopping (R7 and R8 series) signs; (B) Walking/Hitchhiking/Crossing (R9 series, R10-1 through R10-4b) signs; (C) Acknowledgment signs; and (D) Bikeway signs intended for exclusive use by bicyclists or pedestrians. (STOP signs are not among the excludable categories.) Support (informational): - "Compliance with the Standard in Paragraph 2 of this Section is achieved by having a method in place and using the method to maintain the minimum levels established in Table 2A-5. Provided that an assessment or management method is being used, an agency or official having jurisdiction would be in compliance with the Standard in Paragraph 2 of this Section even if there are some individual signs that do not meet the minimum retroreflectivity levels at a particular point in time." Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2A-5, whose White on Red row lists minimum maintained levels of W ≥ 35 and R ≥ 7 cd/lx/m² (measured at 0.2° observation and −4.0° entrance angles), with the footnote requiring a minimum sign contrast ratio ≥ 3:1 (white ÷ red). Citations: - Section 2A.22 Standard §2 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Support §3 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Guidance §4 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Option §5 (p.63) - Table 2A-5 (p.62)
gold_answer: Not automatically. The agency complies by having and using a method designed to maintain the minimums, even if some individual signs fall below them at a particular moment. For white on red, the table gives white at least 35, red at least 7 cd/lx/m², and at least a 3:1 white-to-red contrast ratio.
